newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ANTARCTICA DRIFTS FROM PRETORIA TO CAPE TOWN.
newsitem.headline: ANTARCTICA DRIFTS FROM PRETORIA TO CAPE TOWN.

text.p: The South African city of Cape Town has laid claim to Antarctica, but an official said it was an administrative measure and not part of a bid for the winter Olympics.
The Environment Laws Rationalisation Bill tabled in parliament on Friday proposes:

"For the purposes of the administration of justice and in general for the application of the laws of the republic, Antarctica shall be deemed to be situated within the magisterial district of Cape Town."
Under current South African law, Antarctica, which is managed under an international treaty that forbids any country to claim the continent, is deemed to be part of Pretoria.
A government official said the measure mainly affected the application of justice for South African citizens staffing the country's permanent Antarctic ice station.
"I know Cape Town is bidding for the Olympics in 2004, but I don't think this means they want the Winter Olympics as well," he said.
